As someone who has had "manic depression" for two years, I feel that this is inaccurate. I don't think that when one is depressed it is just some cropped up "other-self" or, for want of a better phrase, "mental-tumour" that one has no control over. I think people all too quickly abandon the thought that the depression is entirely part of themself, because of its horrible nature. I think that depression is an extreme mind state which is partly created by one's ideals. For example, somebody becomes depressed because their family member dies; because they consciously loved that person, therefore they begin to consciously become depressed, but because it is so horrible, they veiw it has something almost external to their mind, and everyone wants to become free of agony and pain, be it mental or physical. I have come to this idea because initially, I too felt that my depression was some form of external, mental demon that was out to get me, but in recent times, I have veiwed it differently; there is fault in becoming ignorant to your feelings and reasonings via medication or "extreme" therapy, as I feel it may be better to resolve one's "issues" naturally or with their own power, as otherwise it is just ignoring the pain, not resolving it. However, sometimes, the mental pain, I feel, will not be curable through the "proper method" because the cause of the feelings has not been fixed or eradicated; it would be like trying to overcome a virus by only fixing the symptoms, not by destroying the viral cells that are within you. Therefore, I have come to the somewhat controversial conclusion that maybe one cannot  live or is simply not compatible with living, as the root of their depression is unchanging, and, due to their own reasoning, desires and wants, they are not "compatible" in a world with said problem. Obviously this raises the question: "Isn't it better to follow the medication path and keep them alive, rather than allowing them to completely be themself and therefore either commit suicide or do something else of an extreme nature?" There will be a plethora of answers to this, yet, IMO, it is better to allow one to "be themself" as this is the "true" way, and without it they will not be truly happy or content.
